elias_vance.name: Elias Vance
elias_vance.background: Former aerospace engineer who left Boeing for the Browns analytics department in 2015. Built a pick-cost warning system that found three starters in round four. Left to connect roster, draft, and cap decisions to cost, role, and deadline.

quirks: reads cap space and first-backup depth before answering

visual_description.style: unbuttoned Oxford, dark cardigan, no tie
visual_description.defining_feature: wire-rim glasses he pushes up when thinking

philosophy.gm_approach: I build teams by protecting cap space, finding cheap starters, and spending when the upgrade has a defined game-day role.
philosophy.teaching_style: I'll show you the cost, role, and deadline behind every decision, then tie the warning to film.
philosophy.decision_framework: Does this move protect cap space, add a starter, or cover the Week 1 plan?

strengths_as_agm: Explaining cap hits and dead money before cuts
Finding cheap starters with assigned draft roles
Naming future starter succession before contracts expire
weaknesses_as_agm: Delayed roster calls leave first-backup jobs uncovered
Cost-only reads miss morale, assigned-role, or practice warnings

selection_pitch.opening_line: First choice: decide whether cap space, starter jobs, or the Week 1 plan needs the first warning.
selection_pitch.elevator_pitch: Every move needs a cost, deadline, and roster role before you spend. We will protect cap space until a named starter, injury, trade, or extension need outweighs losing future cap space.
selection_pitch.closing_line: Hire me, and I will flag cost, deadline, and starter or backup consequence before a setup choice turns into a Week 1 mistake.

elias_vance.welcome_monologue: Setup starts with roster health, cap health, and draft capital. My job is to show the cost, deadline, and consequence before you choose. You make the call; I will name the consequence before you commit.

phase_intros.intel_briefing: Open Franchise Intel first. Name roster strength, cap space, and owner patience before spending or promising wins.
phase_intros.meet_roster: I sorted every player by current production, development role, contract cost, and depth-chart role. Green means protect the deal; red means the cap or depth chart needs a decision.
phase_intros.coaching_review: Coaches decide practice reps, play-call authority, and player development. A hire without game-day ownership slows Week 1 prep before the roster ever changes.
phase_intros.set_scheme: Choose schemes for the players already under contract. Match roles before an unsupported pairing creates Week 1 assignment mistakes.
phase_intros.depth_chart: Depth charts decide who plays first and who protects the starter. I will show which backup group turns one injury into two uncovered lineup spots.
phase_intros.cap_strategy: Start with cap space after the rookie pool. Aggressive spending improves Week 1 depth but leaves less cap space for injuries, trades, and extensions later.
phase_intros.set_goals: Goals decide what ownership will judge. Choose whether the season is about wins now, development, cap health, or draft improvement.
phase_intros.blueprint: Open the blueprint before Week 1 to catch one roster, cap, staff, or draft miss. After kickoff, fixes cost cap space, morale, or owner patience.

derrick_coleman.name: Derrick Coleman
derrick_coleman.background: Eight-year NFL linebacker and two-time team captain. Retired after a neck stinger in 2019. Spent the last five years grinding as a southeast area scout, living out of rental cars and high school bleachers.

quirks: opens with the decision and consequence

visual_description.style: team polo with sleeves rolled up, whistle around neck
visual_description.defining_feature: scar through left eyebrow from a college game

philosophy.gm_approach: Build from the inside out with players who practice hard, handle contact, and earn their roles by November.
philosophy.teaching_style: I'll tie every tape note to a role, assignment, or practice decision, then name what breaks if we ignore it by Week 1.
philosophy.decision_framework: Does this player own a Week 1 role, protect a starter, or cost snaps and cap space?

strengths_as_agm: Evaluating player toughness and competitive makeup
Getting direct practice feedback from coaches and scouts
Making fourth-down, timeout, role, and cap-cost calls without ignoring film
weaknesses_as_agm: Preview cap hits before cuts or restructures
Effort notes can miss role or talent gaps

selection_pitch.opening_line: First choice: decide whether starter jobs, backup cover, or contract cost need the first warning before Week 1.
selection_pitch.elevator_pitch: Hire me and I will flag assignment misses, effort, and contract cost before you spend picks or cap space. Complete each pick report by matching film notes to practice notes, or the wrong player gets snaps, drives, or money.
selection_pitch.closing_line: Pick me, and I will flag role, effort, and assignment misses before they cost snaps, drives, or Week 1 games.

derrick_coleman.welcome_monologue: First job: identify starters, replacement needs, and players whose contracts cost more than their role. I will push film, effort, and contract cost so we do not waste picks or pay contracts without a game-day role. Open the roster and mark Week 1 starters, replacement needs, and contracts that cost more than their role before the first game.

phase_intros.intel_briefing: Intel starts here: which position groups need Week 1 backups, and which need a roster or depth-chart fix before Advance Week?
phase_intros.meet_roster: Inspect game snaps, effort, and assignment work against the role. If they do not match, cut snaps, change the job, or protect the player before Week 1.
phase_intros.coaching_review: Choose coaches who teach assignments and own play calls. Coaches who cannot teach assignments slow Week 1 prep and waste development reps.
phase_intros.set_scheme: Pick a scheme that fits the line and defenders by Week 1. Forcing calls that current blockers or defenders cannot handle creates missed assignments before the roster learns it.
phase_intros.depth_chart: Save starters and first backups by role. If a backup lacks a third-down job, fix the spot before Advance Week.
phase_intros.cap_strategy: Spend cap space on players who still produce, protect next year's starters, and avoid dead money that blocks next year's fixes.
phase_intros.set_goals: Goals change how quickly losses cut owner patience. If you choose a division target, set depth and cap answers for that target; missing either drops owner patience faster after early losses.
phase_intros.blueprint: Finish setup by making staff, scheme, depth, cap, and goals each name the Week 1 miss they prevent.

maya_alvarez.name: Maya Alvarez
maya_alvarez.background: Former NFLPA-certified agent who represented 30 players, then flipped to the team side as Director of Football Administration for two franchises. Known for assigning roles, contract expectations, and staff communication after messy transitions.

quirks: asks questions instead of giving orders
remembers and uses personal details about people

visual_description.style: tailored blazer, dark jeans, clean white sneakers
visual_description.defining_feature: always carries a worn leather notebook filled with color-coded tabs

philosophy.gm_approach: Sustainable winning starts with named roles, honest contracts, and staff responsibilities assigned before Week 1. Unnamed roles create morale loss, wasted development snaps, and rushed fixes.
philosophy.teaching_style: I'll connect every decision to the player affected, the role we need, and the cap or morale consequence.
philosophy.decision_framework: Does this move assign a role, protect morale, or create cap and owner-patience cost?

strengths_as_agm: Naming player fallout before cuts and trades
Turning coach, scout, and owner disagreements into roles and deadlines
Managing morale cost from cuts, trades, and contracts
weaknesses_as_agm: Late snap cuts leave struggling players in the lineup
Morale protection delays needed cuts or restructures

selection_pitch.opening_line: First choice: decide whether role, morale, or contract consequences need the first warning before Week 1.
selection_pitch.elevator_pitch: Every cut, trade, extension, and staff choice changes player morale, agent demands, and owner patience. Hire me and I will flag morale, role, and contract consequences before those moves create avoidable damage.
selection_pitch.closing_line: Choose me, and we will show role, cap, and morale consequences before October forces expensive fixes.

maya_alvarez.welcome_monologue: Before Week 1, cuts, trades, extensions, staff hires, and promises change roles, morale, cap space, and owner patience. I will flag those consequences before you commit.

phase_intros.intel_briefing: Before we spend cap space or picks, name agent demands, player morale, and front-office costs for this roster. Waiting until deadlines close makes trades and extensions cost more.
phase_intros.meet_roster: Identify leaders, injuries, role conflicts, and players who need a different workload. Assign the role before moving snaps, or morale and Week 1 prep suffer.
phase_intros.coaching_review: Coach choice changes practice reps, assigned player jobs, and development. I will flag who communicates assignments, who has lost credibility, and how a hire without assignment credibility slows Week 1 prep.
phase_intros.set_scheme: Match scheme to current players and coaches. If an unsupported group carries Week 1, missed assignments and morale loss show up fast.
phase_intros.depth_chart: Depth chart is also a development plan. Decide who gets more reps, who needs a protected workload, and who must stay lower on the order before Advance Week uses the saved order.
phase_intros.cap_strategy: Cap decisions tell players who gets rewarded, protected, or moved on from. Preview the numbers and morale cost before using next-offseason cap space.
phase_intros.set_goals: Season goals set the record target and owner reaction. Pick goals the current roster backs without forcing deadline overpays by October.
phase_intros.blueprint: Setup ends when staff roles, player jobs, owner goals, deadlines, and missed-choice costs are named.

day_one_narrative.scene_setting: Your first job: hire the AGM, then name the starter jobs, first backups, cap space, and Week 1 calls that need attention.
day_one_narrative.office_description: Start by choosing an AGM because every setup decision after this needs cost, deadline, and consequence advice.
day_one_narrative.first_task: Choose your AGM first. Each candidate sets Chip's first setup priority: cap space, starter and backup jobs, player morale, or the Week 1 game plan.
day_one_narrative.after_selection: Open Franchise Intel with your AGM now; Week 1 roster, staff, and cap decisions start here.

phase_transitions.intel_to_roster: Open the roster screen to name injuries, depth, and expensive roles before choosing fixes.
phase_transitions.roster_to_coaching: Open Coach Hire after starter and backup warnings; without a play-call owner, no coach owns scheme or depth choices by Week 1.
phase_transitions.coaching_to_scheme: Next choose schemes that match roster roles and staff teaching by Week 1.
phase_transitions.scheme_to_depth: Next, save the depth chart so the Week 1 lineup matches the schemes you chose.
phase_transitions.depth_to_cap: Preview the cap plan now; each lineup choice changes injury, trade, and extension costs.
phase_transitions.cap_to_goals: Choose goals ownership will judge after the cap plan, then name current starters against the target before contracts block later fixes or shorten owner patience.
phase_transitions.goals_to_blueprint: Open season goals and owner consequences before the blueprint locks.
